newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Venezuelans fire on Colombian boat, kill boy.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelans fire on Colombian boat, kill boy.

text.p: Venezuelan border guards opened fire on a Colombian boat on Thursday, killing a 3-year-old boy and injuring seven others on the river border between the two countries, officials said.

Colombian Foreign Relations Minister Maria Emma Mejia issued an "energetic" condemnation of the attack, in which a young girl also lost a hand, but did not say whether an official diplomatic protest would be made.

Authorities in the eastern town of Arauquita said the shooting took place after leftist rebels opened fire on the border post in La Victoria in Venezuela's Apure state. Three guards were reported wounded.
Officials from the defence and foreign ministries were sent to investigate the incident.

"This incident is particularly grave because it occurred in international waters. We will be carrying out an investigation and will act rigorously. We will act as we see fit because this incident is unacceptable," Mejia said.

Regional army commander Gen. Rafael Hernandez said he believed the border guards fired on the civilian boat by mistake, fearing it carried rebels of the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force.
Colombia and Venezuela share a 1,300 mile (2,200 km) border, a zone with a heavy guerrilla presence.
